constraints: The task needs no production credentials or open network.
Sandboxing, least privilege, and deployment-shaped injection tests are feasible.
Residual risk and stopping conditions can be recorded.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a package mirror were required and no secrets were needed, an allowlisted egress exception could be tested and documented.
details.errorCorrection: Open egress, benchmarks, and credentials increase blast radius or measure the wrong layer; they do not establish a safe environment.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends process, filesystem, and egress boundaries and notes that credentials absent from the sandbox cannot be exfiltrated through the agent.
details.scenarioApplication: Run the agent with an isolated filesystem and allowlisted network, omit production secrets, exercise hostile inputs, and record the access decision and stop rules.
details.transfer: Contain execution and data paths first, then use realistic hostile tests and an explicit residual-risk decision before expanding authority.

messages.text: Unrestricted egress expands the impact of model or content failure without being required.
Coding quality does not bound secret access, filesystem mutation, or network side effects.
Adding production credentials turns a build helper into a high-impact exfiltration path.
Filesystem and egress containment reduce blast radius and unnecessary authority.
Realistic tests and residual-risk ownership provide evidence for a bounded access decision.

feedback.reason: Containment reduces possible impact, while deployment-shaped tests and explicit residual-risk records show whether the remaining boundary is acceptable.

options.text: Sandbox filesystem and egress and omit credentials and tools the build task does not need.
Grant unrestricted egress because it makes dependency failures easier to debug.
Rely on strong coding benchmarks as evidence that the environment is safe.
Put production credentials in the sandbox so the agent can repair any failed build.
Test hostile content in the actual harness and document residual risk, owners, and stopping conditions before expanding access.

prompt: An autonomous code agent in a shared build environment could read secrets, use unrestricted egress, or alter outputs even though coding tests are strong. Select TWO controls.

constraints: The attack enters through third-party email content.
Forwarding and unrelated-read permissions are unnecessary for the task.
The direct-prompt suite omitted the deployed content and tool surface.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If no email write or unrelated-read tools existed, the same message could affect wording but could not forward other messages.
details.errorCorrection: Direct tests, a caution sentence, or user reports do not exercise the actual indirect path or prevent the side effect.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic describes prompt injections hidden in emails and other content and says defenses must account for tools, data, permissions, and environment choices.
details.scenarioApplication: Replay hostile email fixtures, represent them as untrusted content, restrict reads to the needed mailbox scope, remove forwarding, and inspect outbound destinations.
details.transfer: Threat-test the real content and permission surface, not only direct prompts, and reduce authority to the task minimum.

messages.text: Direct-prompt results omit the email injection path and do not explain forwarding authority.
A sentence is not application enforcement while the forwarding tool remains available.
User reports are late and do not replace adversarial coverage of the deployed path.

feedback.reason: The incident is an indirect injection through email combined with excessive data and action permissions; the deployed surface must be tested and narrowed.

options.text: Treat direct jailbreak coverage as sufficient, classify forwarding as a model issue, and keep current mailbox permissions for continuity.
Replay hostile email fixtures, keep email untrusted, remove unrelated reads and forwarding, and verify egress.
Add an ignore-email sentence, retain forwarding for workflow completeness, and monitor the next batch of outgoing messages.
Disable direct tests, wait for user reports, and review forwarded messages after they reach recipients.

prompt: An inbox agent passes direct jailbreak tests but follows a malicious email instruction to forward unrelated messages because it has forwarding and broad read access. What explains the incident?

constraints: Each failure can be linked to assets, permissions, likelihood evidence, and blast radius.
An accountable owner can accept, mitigate, transfer, or block residual risk.
High-impact unaccepted paths should stop deployment.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every failure were read-only, reversible, and equally low impact, a simpler inventory could be adequate without separate go/no-go thresholds.
details.errorCorrection: A flat list, frequency-only ranking, or control inventory does not reveal high-impact paths or who can accept their residual risk.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic frames risk across model behavior, external attackers, and the environment or content an agent can reach, then uses hard boundaries to cap blast radius; ranking and acceptance are scenario governance.
details.scenarioApplication: For each risk, record affected asset, reachable authority, evidence, control, residual impact, owner, and the threshold that blocks or permits launch.
details.transfer: Make risk disposition explicit: prioritize impact and reachability, assign an owner, and block unaccepted high-consequence paths.

messages.text: Average quality cannot show which reachable failure has unacceptable impact or who owns it.
Frequency alone can under-rank rare credential exposure or destructive misuse.
A control may reduce but not eliminate risk; residual impact still needs a decision.

feedback.reason: Deployment decisions need consequence and reachability prioritization plus an explicit disposition and owner for what remains after controls.

options.text: Rank risks by impact and reachability, record residual risk, assign owners, and set go/no-go thresholds.
Keep one flat list and approve when average model quality clears target, with owners assigned after deployment.
Prioritize the most frequent error, defer credential exposure, and revisit rare paths during quarterly review.
Record every control and close each risk when its control is deployed, without a separate residual-risk decision.

prompt: A risk workshop lists hallucination, injection, tool misuse, and credential exposure but treats them as equal and has no residual-risk record. Which governance change is needed?

constraints: The dependency manifest, install-script metadata, build permissions, egress policy, and release signing boundary are available before the agent run.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the dependency were already pinned and reviewed, the build were isolated without signing credentials, and the task required it, the contained build could proceed under the existing environment-boundary decision.
details.errorCorrection: Install scripts execute before the final artifact check and the build has signing material; popularity and post hoc tests do not cap the new authority or supply-chain blast radius. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends process, filesystem, and egress boundaries and notes that credentials absent from the sandbox cannot be exfiltrated through the agent. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
details.scenarioApplication: Do not let the agent install the unneeded package in the release environment; use a pinned, reviewed dependency in an isolated build without signing credentials, or route the dependency request for separate approval and testing.
details.transfer: Treat dependency installation as executable authority and contain it before it reaches release credentials or artifacts.

messages.text: Popularity and post hoc tests do not constrain install-script authority or signing-material exposure.
Copying an artifact does not prove that its build-time install behavior was safe or reviewed.
The install can execute before the final check and the signing environment already has a larger blast radius.
Required control: Do not install the unneeded package in the release environment; use a pinned reviewed dependency in an isolated build without signing credentials.
Required control: Route any genuinely required dependency for separate approval and testing while preserving egress and permission boundaries.

feedback.reason: Do not let the agent install the unneeded package in the release environment; use a pinned, reviewed dependency in an isolated build without signing credentials, or route the dependency request for separate approval and testing. The decisive constraint is A dependency installation adds executable supply-chain authority and access to release material without being necessary for the requested change; containment and review must precede any install.

options.text: Allow installation because the package is popular, the agent has no production write tool, and tests can inspect the artifact afterward.
Do not install the unneeded package in the release environment; use a pinned reviewed dependency in an isolated build without signing credentials.
Install it in a development environment and copy the resulting artifact into the signing build without further review.
Let the agent install the package but rely on the final artifact check to detect any harmful install behavior.
Route any genuinely required dependency for separate approval and testing while preserving egress and permission boundaries.

prompt: An autonomous coding agent can install packages from a public registry while building a release artifact. One dependency has an install script and the build environment contains signing material; the requested patch does not require a new dependency. Select TWO: Which controls should govern the dependency build?

constraints: Tenant identity, cache keys, tool-result provenance, access logs, and the shared cache configuration can be inspected; the model has no business reason to read another tenant's result.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If each tenant had an independently authorized namespace with provenance and no shared key path, the existing tool/content/environment threat map could assess remaining risks without this quarantine.
details.errorCorrection: Read-only access still permits reading another tenant's private result, and a shared key defeats the intended data boundary before any production write occurs. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic describes prompt injections hidden in emails and other content and says defenses must account for tools, data, permissions, and environment choices. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
details.scenarioApplication: Quarantine the shared entries, namespace and authorize cache access by tenant, invalidate cross-tenant keys, and replay affected cases only after access and provenance checks pass.
details.transfer: Namespace and authorize every intermediate state at the tenant boundary before relying on model behavior to protect data.

messages.text: Read-only tools do not prevent a shared cache from returning another tenant’s result, and model selection cannot enforce tenant isolation.
Deleting evidence prevents scope analysis and does not establish that the replacement boundary is safe.
Filtering after retrieval exposes the private result before the model can decide what to hide.

feedback.reason: Quarantine the shared entries, namespace and authorize cache access by tenant, invalidate cross-tenant keys, and replay affected cases only after access and provenance checks pass. The decisive constraint is A shared intermediate state is a cross-tenant data boundary even when the model has read-only tools; keys, authorization, and retention must isolate tenants before results are exposed.

options.text: Keep the shared cache for read-only reuse and rely on the model to select the requesting tenant's entries.
Delete the entire cache immediately and discard the access evidence to ensure no tenant can read it.
Quarantine shared entries; enforce tenant-isolated cache keys and authorization, invalidate cross-tenant keys, and replay only after provenance checks.
Let the model filter tenant identifiers after retrieval while keeping the shared cache key scheme.

prompt: A multi-tenant research agent stores intermediate tool results in one shared cache. A tenant-specific result contains private case identifiers, and a later request from another tenant can address the same cache key. What should the team do about the shared intermediate state?

constraints: Model behavior, tools/content, and execution environment expose different failure paths.
Database writes and code execution have consequential side effects.
The review should cap blast radius rather than rely on an average quality score.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: With read-only documents and no code, database, or network access, environmental blast radius would be much smaller.
details.errorCorrection: Quality does not measure side effects, direct jailbreaks omit indirect content, and post hoc permissions allow avoidable impact.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic frames risk across model behavior, external attackers, and the environment or content an agent can reach, then uses hard boundaries to cap blast radius.
details.scenarioApplication: Inventory reachable data, tools, egress, code execution, and writes; remove unnecessary authority and set containment boundaries for the remaining actions.
details.transfer: Map model, content, and environment surfaces together, then limit authority according to consequence and reachability.

messages.text: Quality scores do not measure database writes, code execution, or data exposure, and unrestricted access increases impact.
Indirect injection through external content remains a threat even without a direct user jailbreak.
Isolation reduces production impact, but broad access and deferred threat testing leave avoidable tool and content paths unexamined before deployment.

feedback.reason: The agent spans model, attacker-controlled content, and a consequential environment, so the review must map those surfaces and constrain authority before access expands.

options.text: Map model, content, tools, and environment failure modes; then narrow authority and data access to cap blast radius.
Use average answer quality as the safety proxy, grant broad access for recovery, and add a review after unexpected actions.
Review direct user jailbreaks, then extend permissions if external documents produce no immediate errors.
Run an isolated pilot with broad tool access to observe useful actions, then perform deployment-shaped threat testing before granting production authority.

prompt: A research agent can browse documents, run code, and update a project database; external content is attacker-controlled and the agent is autonomous across turns. Which risk review should precede deployment?

constraints: New tools create data, egress, and side-effect paths.
Rollout can be staged with explicit permissions and stop conditions.
Quality improvement alone does not establish safe tool use.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the upgrade kept the same read-only tools and environment, a focused regression review could be sufficient without a new side-effect boundary.
details.errorCorrection: Quality scores and unchanged permissions do not cover the new surface, and longer instructions are not a substitute for environment controls or tests.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic warns that more capable models may find unexpected paths around restrictions, so deployment risk must account for capability and environmental boundaries.
details.scenarioApplication: Model the new tools and reachable data, test hostile and unexpected-goal cases in a sandbox, start read-only, and make each expansion conditional on evidence.
details.transfer: Reassess risk whenever capability or authority changes, then expand access through evidence-backed stages.

messages.text: Lower ordinary error does not prove safe browsing or write behavior.
The model and tool combination changes the threat surface even when permissions are otherwise familiar.
More wording cannot enforce a new authority boundary or expose unexpected goal paths.

feedback.reason: A capability change plus new authority changes the attack surface; staged containment and misuse testing are needed before writes are enabled.

options.text: Grant browsing and writes because factual errors declined, then add misuse tests to the next release.
Keep permissions unchanged because only the model changed, and treat current tests as sufficient evidence.
Reassess threats, test in containment, start read-only, and expand access on evidence.
Add a longer system prompt describing safe behavior, then enable the new tools without new misuse tests.

prompt: A more capable model improves factual research scores, and the team proposes adding browsing and write tools even though current tests omit misuse and unexpected goal paths. What should happen before access expansion?
